title: Running MBIST through IJTAG
summary: Time to connect this training to the previous ones: the MBIST controllers of *MBIST Architecture* sit in an IJTAG network behind the chip's TAP. This topic follows a complete MBIST run from the tester, through the TAP and the network, to the controller and back.
objectives: Describe the test data register of an MBIST controller.
Write the sequence of TAP operations that runs one MBIST test.
Compute how long the tester waits in Run-Test/Idle.
Explain how many controllers are run together, and how test access is protected in the field.

blocks.caption: Configuration fields are written, status fields are captured and read

blocks.md: An MBIST controller appears in the IJTAG network as one or more **TDRs** behind a SIB. The tester **writes** configuration — which algorithm, which background, diagnosis on or off, *start* — and **reads** status — *done*, *pass*, and diagnosis data such as the failing address. Thanks to capture-shift-update, one scan can write the next configuration and read the last status.

subsections.title: One MBIST run, step by step

steps.title: IR scan
steps.md: Load the TAP instruction that connects the IJTAG network between TDI and TDO.

steps.title: Open the path
steps.md: A DR scan writes the SIBs that lead to the MBIST controller.

steps.title: Configure and start
steps.md: A DR scan writes algorithm, background and **start = 1**. In Update-DR the controller sees start and begins.

steps.title: Wait
steps.md: The tester keeps the TAP in **Run-Test/Idle** for a given number of TCK clocks. Meanwhile the March test runs on the **memory clock**.

steps.title: Read the result
steps.md: A DR scan captures **done** and **pass** and shifts them out. The tester compares them with the expected values: done = 1, pass = 1.

blocks.code:
# PDL for the controller (simplified illustration, see Topic 7)
iProc run_march {} {
  iWrite algorithm  MarchCminus
  iWrite background 0
  iWrite start      1
  iApply
  iRunLoop 1100000 -tck      ;# wait in Run-Test/Idle
  iRead  done 1
  iRead  pass 1
  iApply
}

blocks.md:
The tester does not watch the test; it simply waits long enough and then reads *done*. The wait is counted in **TCK clocks**:

> wait (TCK clocks) ≥ test time × f(TCK)

Example: March C− on a 1 Mi-word memory at 100 MHz takes 105 ms. With TCK = 10 MHz the tester waits at least 0.105 s × 10 MHz ≈ **1.05 million** TCK clocks — the PDL above uses 1.1 million for margin.

blocks.title: Why not poll done?
blocks.md: Polling — reading *done* again and again — is possible, but every read is a DR scan, and on a tester every branch on a result costs time. Production programs prefer a fixed, safe wait followed by a single read.

subsections.title: Many controllers, and access in the field

items.title: Starting many controllers together
items.md: Open the SIBs of all controllers of one test session and write their configuration in **one** scan; their *start* bits all take effect in the same Update-DR. After the wait, one scan reads every *done* and *pass*.

items.title: Reading diagnosis data
items.md: Fail addresses are read only when a memory fails. Opening just that controller's SIB keeps the path short.

items.title: Access in the field
items.md: In a car or a server, the chip's own software may run MBIST through the **same IJTAG network**, reached from an on-chip bus instead of the TAP pins. The *BIST in the Field* training covers this.

items.title: Security
items.md: Test access can read and write almost anything in the chip. Production parts therefore **lock** the TAP or parts of the network (fuses, passwords, challenge-response) so that attackers cannot use it.

questions.text: Sort the MBIST register fields: written by the tester or read by the tester?
Put the steps of an MBIST run through JTAG in order.
items: IR scan: select the IJTAG network
DR scan: open the SIB path
DR scan: write configuration and start
DR scan: read done and pass

questions.text: A memory test takes 20 ms. TCK runs at 25 MHz. At least how many TCK clocks must the tester wait?
While the tester waits in Run-Test/Idle, which clock runs the March test?
How can several MBIST controllers be started at exactly the same time?
options: Write all their start bits in one DR scan; they take effect together in Update-DR
Start them one per IR scan
Use a separate TAP for each

questions.text: Production chips often lock test access, because an open TAP could let an attacker read or change the chip's internals.
